books.title: The Civil War in France
books.author: Karl Marx
books.shortDescription: Written by Karl Marx between April and May 1871 as an official address to the General Council of the International Workingmen's Association, The Civil War in France is Marx's seminal historical materialist analysis of the Paris Commune. Written while Communards were defending Paris against Versaillist troops, Marx synthesizes the lessons of the first working-class government in history, establishing the core Marxist proposition that the working class cannot simply lay hold of the ready-made state machinery and wield it for its own purposes, but must smash the bourgeois state apparatus and replace it with genuine proletarian democracy.
books.subject: State Theory & Dictatorship of the Proletariat

books.title: Communism and the Family
books.author: Alexandra Kollontai
books.shortDescription: First published in 1920 during the Russian Civil War, Communism and the Family is Alexandra Kollontai's landmark pamphlet on Marxist feminism and social transformation. Kollontai demonstrates how industrial capitalism destroyed the self-contained domestic economy, pulling women into wage labor while leaving them burdened with unpaid housework. She outlines how a socialist society replaces private domestic isolation with collective kitchens, laundries, and communal childcare, liberating women to participate fully in economic and political life as equal human beings.
books.subject: Marxist Feminism

books.title: The Communist Manifesto
books.author: Karl Marx & Friedrich Engels
books.shortDescription: Commissioned by the Communist League and published in London in February 1848, this pamphlet was written during a period of massive political unrest across Europe. It explains the class struggle and critiques capitalism, serving as a call to action for the working class.
books.subject: Class Struggle

books.title: Capital: Volume 1 (The Process of Production of Capital)
books.author: Karl Marx
books.shortDescription: First published in 1867, Volume 1 of Marx's magnum opus analyzes the capitalist mode of production, commodity fetishism, surplus value, wage labor, and primitive accumulation.
books.subject: Political Economy

books.title: Capital: Volume 2 (The Process of Circulation of Capital)
books.author: Karl Marx (ed. Friedrich Engels)
books.shortDescription: Edited by Friedrich Engels and published posthumously in 1885, Volume 2 examines the circulation of capital, turnover times, reproduction schemes, and macro-economic circuit dynamics.
books.subject: Political Economy

books.title: Capital: Volume 3 (The Process of Capitalist Production as a Whole)
books.author: Karl Marx (ed. Friedrich Engels)
books.shortDescription: Published in 1894 by Engels, Volume 3 synthesizes production and circulation to explain profit equalization, the tendency of the rate of profit to fall, credit, fictitious capital, and ground rent.
books.subject: Political Economy

books.title: Critique of the Gotha Programme
books.author: Karl Marx
books.shortDescription: Written by Karl Marx in 1875 as marginal notes on the draft program of the united German Social Democratic Workers' Party, this seminal text details the transition from capitalism to lower and higher phases of communist society.
books.subject: Classical Marxism

books.title: Grundrisse
books.author: Karl Marx
books.shortDescription: Written in 1857-1858, the Grundrisse (German for 'Outlines') is a massive set of raw, private notebooks where Marx worked out his economic theories before writing Capital. Left unpublished until 1939, it contains Marx's most futuristic speculations on automation, technology, and the liberation of human free time.
books.subject: Political Economy

books.title: On Guerrilla Warfare
books.author: Mao Zedong
books.shortDescription: First published in 1937 during the Second Sino-Japanese War while Mao Zedong was based in Yan'an, this seminal treatise outlines the military and political doctrine of protracted guerrilla warfare. Mao establishes that guerrilla warfare is not merely a military tactic, but a political struggle of the masses against a foreign invader or oppressive ruling class, requiring deep integration with the population.
books.subject: Anti-Imperialism

books.title: Imperialism, the Highest Stage of Capitalism
books.author: V.I. Lenin
books.shortDescription: Written in Zurich in early 1916, during World War I, and first published as a pamphlet in mid-1917 in Petrograd. Lenin wrote it under tsarist censorship, forcing him to use cautious, 'Aesopian' language and focus on purely economic analysis. The work builds on J.A. Hobson's and Rudolf Hilferding's studies of imperialism and finance capital, synthesising their data into a Marxist framework that explains imperialism as a necessary stage of capitalist development, not merely a policy choice.
books.subject: Anti-Imperialism

books.title: “Left-Wing” Communism: an Infantile Disorder
books.author: V.I. Lenin
books.shortDescription: Written in 1920 for the Second Congress of the Communist International, Lenin's classic treatise critiques sectarian 'left' radicalism and outlines pragmatic, principled revolutionary strategy and tactics.
books.subject: Party Strategy & Tactics

books.title: On Contradiction
books.author: Mao Zedong
books.shortDescription: A simplified guide to Mao Zedong's essay on how conflict and change work. It explains why opposing forces exist in everything and how focusing on the main problem helps solve real-life challenges.
books.subject: Dialectics

books.title: The Origin of the Family, Private Property and the State
books.author: Friedrich Engels
books.shortDescription: Published in 1884 following Karl Marx's death, this landmark work draws on Lewis H. Morgan's anthropological research into Indigenous societies to demonstrate that social institutions like the monogamous family, private property, and the state are not eternal features of human existence, but historical developments that arose alongside class division.
books.subject: Anthropology

books.title: The Principles of Communism
books.author: Friedrich Engels
books.shortDescription: Drafted by Friedrich Engels in 1847 as a 25-question catechism for the Communist League, this foundational work provides clear, accessible answers explaining the core principles of Marxism.
books.subject: Classical Marxism

books.title: Prostitution and Ways of Fighting It
books.author: Alexandra Kollontai
books.shortDescription: Delivered as a speech to the Third All-Russian Conference of Heads of Regional Women's Departments in 1921, Prostitution and Ways of Fighting It is Alexandra Kollontai's groundbreaking Marxist analysis of sex work and Soviet social policy. Kollontai argues that prostitution is rooted in capitalist poverty and female economic dependence, defining prostitutes not as criminals or fallen women, but as labor deserters alongside non-working kept wives. She outlines Soviet strategies to eradicate prostitution through vocational training, economic equality, public health, and free comradeship.
books.subject: Marxist Feminism

books.title: Red Love
books.author: Alexandra Kollontai
books.shortDescription: Published in 1927, Red Love (Vasilisa Malygina) is Alexandra Kollontai's pioneering revolutionary novel set during the New Economic Policy (NEP) in Soviet Russia. The novel dramatizes the conflict between the new communist morality of female economic independence and the revival of bourgeois careerism and possessiveness. Following Vasilisa, a devoted Bolshevik textile worker, the narrative explores the breakdown of her marriage to Volodya as he succumbs to NEP-era bureaucratization and bourgeois corruption, illustrating the necessity for working women to build self-reliance through socialized labor and revolutionary comradeship.
books.subject: Marxist Feminism

books.title: Reform or Revolution
books.author: Rosa Luxemburg
books.shortDescription: First published in 1899-1900 as a polemic against Eduard Bernstein's revisionist reformism, Social Reform or Revolution is Rosa Luxemburg's masterwork defending scientific socialism. Luxemburg demonstrates that trade unions and legislative reforms cannot gradually dissolve capitalist exploitation, proving that reform and revolution are not optional pathways to the same goal, but fundamental choices between repairing capitalism or abolishing wage slavery.
books.subject: Marxist Political Economy

books.title: Sexual Relations and the Class Struggle
books.author: Alexandra Kollontai
books.shortDescription: Written in 1921, Sexual Relations and the Class Struggle is Alexandra Kollontai's foundational theoretical essay applying historical materialism to sexual morality, marriage, and human psychology. Kollontai demonstrates how sexual ethics evolve alongside economic modes of production, tracing the transition from feudal tribalism to bourgeois individualistic possessiveness. She argues that capitalist atomization produces acute spiritual loneliness and possessive marital rights, urging the revolutionary working class to forge a new sexual code based on comradely solidarity, female independence, and collective class unity.
books.subject: Marxist Feminism

books.title: The Social Basis of the Woman Question
books.author: Alexandra Kollontai
books.shortDescription: First published in 1909, The Social Basis of the Woman Question is Alexandra Kollontai's landmark text drawing a sharp materialist distinction between bourgeois feminism and proletarian women's liberation. Kollontai demonstrates that while bourgeois feminists seek equal privileges with men within the existing capitalist framework, working women seek to abolish economic slavery alongside male comrades through socialized labor, universal childcare, and revolutionary transformation.
books.subject: Marxist Feminism

books.title: The Attitude of the Workers' Party to Religion
books.author: V.I. Lenin
books.shortDescription: Published in Proletary in May 1909 during a period of reaction following the defeat of the 1905 Russian Revolution, The Attitude of the Workers' Party to Religion is V.I. Lenin's classic treatise on dialectical materialism and religious policy. Lenin addresses debates in the Russian Duma and within the Bolshevik party, explaining why Marxists are absolute philosophical materialists yet oppose anarchistic declarations of war on religion, insisting that atheist education must be subordinated to the practical class struggle.
books.subject: Marxist Philosophy & Party Strategy

books.title: A Great Love
books.author: Alexandra Kollontai
books.shortDescription: First published in 1929, A Great Love is Alexandra Kollontai's acclaimed collection of three novellas: A Great Love, Sisters, and The Loves of Three Generations. Through intimate narrative studies of Bolshevik revolutionaries, working mothers, and changing familial standards, Kollontai explores the psychological dilemmas facing women during the transition to socialism. The title story dramatizes the emotional friction between a devoted female organizer and her male comrade, while Sisters and Three Generations examine workplace exploitation, single motherhood, and the evolution of sexual morality across successive generations.
books.subject: Marxist Feminism

books.title: The Holy Family
books.author: Karl Marx & Friedrich Engels
books.shortDescription: Published in 1845, The Holy Family, or Critique of Critical Critique was the first major collaborative work by Karl Marx and Friedrich Engels. Written as a polemic against Bruno Bauer and the Young Hegelian 'Critical Critics', the text marks a decisive turning point in the development of scientific socialism. Marx and Engels demolish speculative Hegelian idealism, formulate the historic mission of the proletariat to abolish private property, trace the philosophical roots of socialism to 18th-century French materialism, and establish Charles Fourier's principle that women's emancipation is the natural measure of general social freedom.
books.subject: Marxist Philosophy & Historical Materialism

books.title: Theses on Communist Morality in the Sphere of Marital Relations
books.author: Alexandra Kollontai
books.shortDescription: First published in Kommunistka (No. 12, 1921), Theses on Communist Morality in the Sphere of Marital Relations presents Alexandra Kollontai's definitive guidelines for revolutionary personal ethics. Kollontai demonstrates that as the workers' state assumes responsibility for public dining, laundries, and child welfare, human relationships are liberated from economic dependence, proprietary jealousy, and commercial marriage contracts, enabling true emotional solidarity.
books.subject: Marxist Feminism

books.title: Value, Price and Profit
books.author: Karl Marx
books.shortDescription: First published in 1865, this text forms an essential part of Karl Marx's critique of political economy. It provides simplified, yet rigorous, explanations of key capitalist economic concepts.
books.subject: Political Economy

books.title: Wage Labour and Capital
books.author: Karl Marx
books.shortDescription: Based on lectures Marx delivered in 1847 to the German Workingmen's Club in Brussels, this work provides a straightforward and accessible explanation of the economic relationships under capitalism, particularly how labor becomes a commodity and how wages are determined.
books.subject: Political Economy

books.title: What Is To Be Done?
books.author: V.I. Lenin
books.shortDescription: Lenin's seminal work on political organization, arguing that working-class political consciousness requires systematic theoretical education rather than pure trade unionism.
books.subject: Party Organization

books.title: Women's Suffrage and Class Struggle
books.author: Rosa Luxemburg
books.shortDescription: Delivered at the Second Social Democratic Women's Rally in Stuttgart, Germany on May 12, 1912, Women's Suffrage and Class Struggle is Rosa Luxemburg's classic speech demonstrating why working-class women's vote is a revolutionary threat to the capitalist state. Luxemburg contrasts working women—who create capitalist surplus value in factories and farms—with bourgeois women who act as co-consumers of surplus value, proving that the struggle for women's suffrage is an integral part of the proletarian revolution.
books.subject: Marxist Feminism
